sense: of a mirror, water or light

terms.gloss: reflect, throw back (light, an image, a sound)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: not before Augustus. Mostly in the passive participle: light repercussum, an image repercussa, and of sound, valleys repercussae that echo the shouting (Liv. 21.33.6).

evidence: Ov. Met. 2.110: clāra repercussō reddēbant lūmina Phoebō (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: a reflection, an image (in a mirror or water)
evidence: Varro LL 6.82: speculum, quod in eō specimus imāginem

phrases.latin: sīcut aquae tremulum labrīs ubi lūmen aēnīs sōle repercussum aut radiantis imāgine lūnae omnia pervolitat lātē loca, jamque sub aurās ērigitur summīque ferit laqueāria tēctī
phrases.english: as when the trembling light of water in bronze basins, thrown back by the sun or by the image of the shining moon, flits far and wide over everything, rises into the air and strikes the panels of the ceiling high above

phrases.latin: canis per flūmen carnem cum ferret natāns lymphārum in speculō vīdit simulācrum suum
phrases.english: a dog swimming across a river with a piece of meat saw his reflection in the mirror of the water

phrases.latin: ista repercussae, quam cernis, imāginis umbra est
phrases.english: what you see is the shadow of a reflected image

sources: Lewis & Short: repercutio · Lewis & Short: reddo · Lewis & Short: imago · Lewis & Short: simulacrum
